wire.body:
WS-Federation 1.2 — passive requestor endpoint

Issuer http:///realm/wswire at http:///realm/wswire/wsfed

This endpoint takes a wa parameter, by GET or by form POST, and signs a browser in to a relying party by POSTing it a token (section 13.2.2). It authenticates nobody itself: the username typed at the sign-in screen becomes the subject of the assertion, and in development mode no password is checked.

Try it

  • /FederationMetadata/2007-06/FederationMetadata.xml — the signed federation metadata, which is what a relying party should be configured from.
  • /wsfed/metadata/{rp} — one registered relying party's own metadata (#494), naming the entityID its assertions are issued under: <entityID>:<application>, the name SAML 2.0 and WS-Trust give the same application. A wtrealm nobody registered gets the shared one.

Sign-in request parameters (section 13.2.1)

ParameterWhat this service does with it
waRequired. wsignin1.0, wsignout1.0 or wsignoutcleanup1.0.
wtrealmRequired for sign-in. The relying party's identifier, and the assertion's audience restriction.
wreplyWhere the response is POSTed. Optional — with none it goes to the wsfedReplyUrl registered on the wtrealm's application entry, and with none registered the request is refused. In development mode, which this realm is in, it is not validated against any registration, like every other return URL here.
wctxEchoed back byte for byte and never interpreted. It is the relying party's state.
wctThe request timestamp. Recorded with its skew from this clock; not enforced.
wfreshThe maximum age of the authentication, in MINUTES. 0 forces the screen; N re-shows it when the session authenticated longer than N minutes ago.
wauthThe authentication method demanded. A password method is honoured; a HARDWARE TOKEN one is met by a security key in either role; a MULTI-FACTOR one only by two real factors, so a passwordless key does not answer it. A session that does not meet either is a STEP-UP: the person is sent to sign in again with a second factor required, and the assertion reports the method that actually happened. Still unmet after that one attempt, the request is refused. http://schemas.openid.net/pape/policies/2007/06/phishing-resistant and http://schemas.openid.net/acr/2016/07/phishing-resistant-hardware are a passkey step-up of the same one trip. The second is met only when the realm records the key as hardware-protected. The assertion carries the class the session earned, and otherwise the method it has always reported. Any other value is refused rather than answered with a claim that did not happen.
whrThe home realm. Recorded and shown on the screen; this service is the only identity provider here, so nothing is forwarded.
wreqAn RST by value. Its TokenType selects the token; an AppliesTo that disagrees with wtrealm is logged, and wtrealm wins.
wreqptrRefused. It names a URL for the identity provider to fetch, and fetching an arbitrary URL from a query parameter is a server-side request forgery.
wp, wencodingRecorded in the log. No policy is enforced.
tokenType, trustNON-SPEC, in the manner of /sts?encrypt=1: tokenType=saml2 asks for a SAML 2.0 assertion instead of the SAML 1.1 default, and trust=1.3 wraps it in a ws-sx 200512 RSTR Collection instead of a 2005/02 RequestSecurityTokenResponse.
Not implemented, and stated rather than left to be discovered: wresultptr (the response is always by value), the attribute and pseudonym services (wattr1.0, wpseudo1.0, both answered 501), token encryption in this profile (there is no recipient certificate in a passive request to encrypt to — /sts?encrypt=1 has one because a WS-Security signature carries it), and the WS-Federation metadata exchange over SOAP.

WS-Federation 1.2 section 13.2.2 — the token travels in a form POST, not in a redirect, so it is not length-limited and never appears in a URL, a log or a Referer header.

wa: wsignin1.0
posting to (wreply): https://rp.wswire.test/reply
realm (wtrealm): https://rp.wswire.test/app
token type: urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion
wctx: the request carried none, so none is returned
The form submits itself from /wsfed/autopost.js. It is a separate resource because this service sets script-src 'none' on every response and this page relaxes it to 'self' — an inline script would not run, and the button would be the only thing that worked. With scripting off, the button IS the mechanism.

wire.body:
Language English

This sign-in could not be completed

The application asked for a way of signing in (wauth) that this service does not offer.

What it accepts

  • urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.0:am:password
  • urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.0:am:unspecified
  • urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:ac:classes:PasswordProtectedTransport
  • urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:ac:classes:Password
  • http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/authenticationmethod/password
  • http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2008/06/identity/authenticationmethod/password
  • http://schemas.microsoft.com/claims/multipleauthn
  • urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.0:am:HardwareToken
  • http://schemas.openid.net/pape/policies/2007/06/phishing-resistant
  • http://schemas.openid.net/acr/2016/07/phishing-resistant-hardware

It refuses rather than answering with a password sign-in on purpose: wauth is how a relying party demands a method, and ignoring it would make the demand appear to have been met.

Why am I seeing this page?
WS-Federation defines no error response for a sign-in request: the request is a browser navigation, so there is nothing to send an error back to, and this page is the answer. Nothing has been sent to the relying party.

Close this tab and start again from the application you were using. If this happens again, send the diagnostics below to whoever runs that application.

This request carries wreqptr, which names a URL the identity provider is meant to fetch the request from. Send the request in wreq by value instead.

Summary

Detail
wattr1.0 is the attribute service (section 3.2/13.3): a relying party asking the identity provider for more claims about a subject it already has a token for. It is not implemented here, and it is named rather than silently rejected because "unknown wa" would send someone looking for a typo. wire.body:
WS-Federation 1.2 — passive requestor endpoint

Issuer http:///realm/wswirep at http:///realm/wswirep/wsfed

This endpoint takes a wa parameter, by GET or by form POST, and signs a browser in to a relying party by POSTing it a token (section 13.2.2). It authenticates nobody itself: the person signs in at the sign-in screen, and the identity verified there becomes the subject of the assertion.

Try it

  • /FederationMetadata/2007-06/FederationMetadata.xml — the signed federation metadata, which is what a relying party should be configured from.
  • /wsfed/metadata/{rp} — one registered relying party's own metadata (#494), naming the entityID its assertions are issued under: <entityID>:<application>, the name SAML 2.0 and WS-Trust give the same application. A wtrealm nobody registered gets the shared one.

Sign-in request parameters (section 13.2.1)

ParameterWhat this service does with it
waRequired. wsignin1.0, wsignout1.0 or wsignoutcleanup1.0.
wtrealmRequired for sign-in. The relying party's identifier, and the assertion's audience restriction.
wreplyWhere the response is POSTed. This realm is in PRODUCT mode, so it must be one of the wsfedReplyUrl values on the wtrealm's application entry, compared exactly; with none, the registered one is used.
wctxEchoed back byte for byte and never interpreted. It is the relying party's state.
wctThe request timestamp. Recorded with its skew from this clock; not enforced.
wfreshThe maximum age of the authentication, in MINUTES. 0 forces the screen; N re-shows it when the session authenticated longer than N minutes ago.
wauthThe authentication method demanded. A password method is honoured; a HARDWARE TOKEN one is met by a security key in either role; a MULTI-FACTOR one only by two real factors, so a passwordless key does not answer it. A session that does not meet either is a STEP-UP: the person is sent to sign in again with a second factor required, and the assertion reports the method that actually happened. Still unmet after that one attempt, the request is refused. http://schemas.openid.net/pape/policies/2007/06/phishing-resistant and http://schemas.openid.net/acr/2016/07/phishing-resistant-hardware are a passkey step-up of the same one trip. The second is met only when the realm records the key as hardware-protected. The assertion carries the class the session earned, and otherwise the method it has always reported. Any other value is refused rather than answered with a claim that did not happen.
whrThe home realm. Recorded and shown on the screen; this service is the only identity provider here, so nothing is forwarded.
wreqAn RST by value. Its TokenType selects the token; an AppliesTo that disagrees with wtrealm is logged, and wtrealm wins.
wreqptrRefused. It names a URL for the identity provider to fetch, and fetching an arbitrary URL from a query parameter is a server-side request forgery.
wp, wencodingRecorded in the log. No policy is enforced.
tokenType, trustNON-SPEC, in the manner of /sts?encrypt=1: tokenType=saml2 asks for a SAML 2.0 assertion instead of the SAML 1.1 default, and trust=1.3 wraps it in a ws-sx 200512 RSTR Collection instead of a 2005/02 RequestSecurityTokenResponse.
Not implemented, and stated rather than left to be discovered: wresultptr (the response is always by value), the attribute and pseudonym services (wattr1.0, wpseudo1.0, both answered 501), token encryption in this profile (there is no recipient certificate in a passive request to encrypt to — /sts?encrypt=1 has one because a WS-Security signature carries it), and the WS-Federation metadata exchange over SOAP.

wire.body:
Language English

This sign-in could not be completed

The application asked for a way of signing in (wauth) that this service does not offer.

What it accepts

  • urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.0:am:password
  • urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.0:am:unspecified
  • urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:ac:classes:PasswordProtectedTransport
  • urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:ac:classes:Password
  • http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/authenticationmethod/password
  • http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2008/06/identity/authenticationmethod/password
  • http://schemas.microsoft.com/claims/multipleauthn
  • urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.0:am:HardwareToken
  • http://schemas.openid.net/pape/policies/2007/06/phishing-resistant
  • http://schemas.openid.net/acr/2016/07/phishing-resistant-hardware

It refuses rather than answering with a password sign-in on purpose: wauth is how a relying party demands a method, and ignoring it would make the demand appear to have been met.

Why am I seeing this page?
WS-Federation defines no error response for a sign-in request: the request is a browser navigation, so there is nothing to send an error back to, and this page is the answer. Nothing has been sent to the relying party.

Close this tab and start again from the application you were using. If this happens again, send the diagnostics below to whoever runs that application.
